```{r setup}
#| echo: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(mstate2); library(dplyr) })
options(width = 100, digits = 4, pillar.print_min = 12)
load(Sys.getenv("MSTATE2_DIVINE_DATA", "MSM_Data.RData"))
pct <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%")

# Data, counts and fits used across the slides (each step is also shown where it is introduced)
segs   <- c(NSP = "t.nosp", SP = "t.sp", NIMV = "t.nimv", IMV = "t.mv", Recov = "t.recov")
absb   <- c(Disch = "disch.s", Death = "death.s")
states <- c("NSP", "SP", "Recov", "NIMV", "IMV", "Disch", "Death")
x   <- msprep2(MSM, durations = segs, outcome = absb, states = states)
d   <- prep2(x)
fit <- P2est(d)

# First-order chain: the second-order counts pooled over the previous state h
first_order <- function(d) {
  N1 <- d$N |> summarise(N = sum(N), .by = c("j", "l"))
  Y1 <- d$Y |> summarise(Y = sum(Y), .by = "j")
  est <- left_join(N1, Y1, by = "j") |> mutate(p = N / Y)
  P1 <- matrix(0, length(d$states), length(d$states), dimnames = list(d$states, d$states))
  P1[cbind(as.character(est$j), as.character(est$l))] <- est$p
  P1[cbind(d$absorbing, d$absorbing)] <- 1
  P1
}
P1 <- first_order(d)
T1 <- array(P1, c(7, 7, 7), dimnames = list(states, states, states))   # P[j, l, h] = P1[j, l] for every h
est <- function(h, j, l) filter(fit$estimate, h == !!h, j == !!j, l == !!l)
e_nsp <- est("NSP", "SP", "NIMV"); e_sp <- est("SP", "SP", "NIMV")
p1_nimv <- P1["SP", "NIMV"]
n_first  <- sum(P1 > 0 & row(P1) != col(P1)) + sum(diag(P1) > 0 & !(states %in% d$absorbing))

# Stacked state-occupation plot of an n-step distribution (rows = steps 1..n, columns = states)
state_cols <- c(NSP = "#9ecae1", SP = "#4292c6", Recov = "#a1d99b", NIMV = "#fdae6b",
                IMV = "#e6550d", Disch = "#31a354", Death = "#636363")
stack_plot <- function(Pn, j, main = "", legend = TRUE) {
  start <- setNames(as.numeric(colnames(Pn) == j), colnames(Pn))
  Pn <- rbind(start, Pn)                                   # step 0: the current state
  n  <- 0:(nrow(Pn) - 1)
  cum <- t(apply(Pn, 1, cumsum))
  op <- par(mar = c(4, 4, 2.5, if (legend) 6.5 else 1), xpd = FALSE); on.exit(par(op))
  plot(NA, xlim = range(n), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
       xlab = "days ahead (n)", ylab = "probability", main = main)
  low <- rep(0, length(n))
  for (s in colnames(Pn)) {
    polygon(c(n, rev(n)), c(cum[, s], rev(low)), col = state_cols[s], border = "white", lwd = 0.5)
    low <- cum[, s]
  }
  if (legend) {
    par(xpd = TRUE)
    legend(max(n) * 1.02, 1, legend = rev(colnames(Pn)), fill = rev(state_cols[colnames(Pn)]),
           bty = "n", cex = 0.85, border = "white")
  }
}

# Legend of the stacked plots, drawn in its own panel
state_legend <- function() {
  op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)); on.exit(par(op))
  plot.new()
  legend("left", legend = rev(names(state_cols)), fill = rev(state_cols), bty = "n", border = "white")
}

# State diagram of DIVINE: boxes for the states, arrows for the observed one-step moves
moves <- x$panel |>
  mutate(from = lag(state), .by = "id") |>
  filter(!is.na(from), from != state) |>
  distinct(from, to = state) |>
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
state_diagram <- function(moves) {
  pos <- rbind(NSP = c(0, 2), SP = c(2, 2), NIMV = c(4, 3.2), IMV = c(4, 0.8),
               Recov = c(6, 2.4), Disch = c(8, 3.6), Death = c(8, 0.4))
  hw <- 0.62; hh <- 0.3
  op <- par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0)); on.exit(par(op))
  plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = c(-0.8, 8.8), ylim = c(-0.55, 4.65), asp = 1)
  clip_box <- function(p, q) {                     # point where the segment p -> q leaves the box of p
    v <- q - p; t <- min(hw / abs(v[1]), hh / abs(v[2])); p + t * v
  }
  col_a <- "#4C6FB5"
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(moves))) {
    a <- moves$from[k]; b <- moves$to[k]
    if (a == "NSP" && b == "Disch") {              # around the top
      lines(c(0, 0, 8), c(2 + hh, 4.45, 4.45), col = col_a, lwd = 2)
      arrows(8, 4.45, 8, 3.6 + hh, length = 0.1, col = col_a, lwd = 2)
    } else if (a == "NSP" && b == "Death") {       # around the bottom
      lines(c(0, 0, 8), c(2 - hh, -0.35, -0.35), col = col_a, lwd = 2)
      arrows(8, -0.35, 8, 0.4 - hh, length = 0.1, col = col_a, lwd = 2)
    } else {
      p <- clip_box(pos[a, ], pos[b, ]); q <- clip_box(pos[b, ], pos[a, ])
      arrows(p[1], p[2], q[1], q[2], length = 0.1, col = col_a, lwd = 2)
    }
  }
  for (s in rownames(pos)) {
    ab <- s %in% c("Disch", "Death")
    rect(pos[s, 1] - hw, pos[s, 2] - hh, pos[s, 1] + hw, pos[s, 2] + hh,
         col = if (ab) "#1E2761" else "#e8ecf6", border = "#1E2761", lwd = 2)
    text(pos[s, 1], pos[s, 2], s, col = if (ab) "white" else "#1E2761", font = 2, cex = 1.25)
  }
}
```

## DIVINE through first-order eyes

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r diagram}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.2
state_diagram(moves)
```

**DIVINE**: `r nrow(MSM)` patients hospitalised with COVID-19, followed daily.
`NSP`/`SP` non-severe/severe pneumonia · `NIMV`/`IMV` non-invasive/invasive ventilation · `Recov` recovery · `Disch` · `Death`.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
First-order probabilities for a patient in `SP` **today**:

```{r p1-sp}
#| echo: false
p1_sp <- P1["SP", P1["SP", ] > 0]
knitr::kable(data.frame(tomorrow = names(p1_sp), probability = round(p1_sp, 3)),
             row.names = FALSE, align = "lr")
```

::: {.key}
Under first order, every patient in `SP` today has probability **`r round(p1_nimv, 3)`** of non-invasive ventilation
tomorrow, whatever happened before.
:::
:::
:::

## What we already do: first-order models

$$
P\big(X_s = \ell \mid X_{s-1} = j,\; X_{s-2},\; \dots\big) \;=\; P\big(X_s = \ell \mid X_{s-1} = j\big) \;=\; P_{j\ell}
$$

The future depends on the past **only through the current state**.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.box}
**Continuous time** (`mstate`)

One hazard per transition, Cox models, Aalen–Johansen probabilities.

```r
msd <- msprep(time, status, data, tmat)
cx  <- coxph(Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status) ~
               strata(trans), data = msd)
pt  <- probtrans(msfit(cx, trans = tmat), 0)
```
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.box}
**Discrete time** (days)

One transition matrix, estimated by pooled counts; predictions by matrix powers:

$$
\hat P_{j\ell} = \frac{\sum_s N_{j\ell}(s)}{\sum_s Y_{j}(s-1)},
\qquad
\mathbf P(n) = \mathbf P^{\,n}
$$
:::
:::
:::

## Example: first order, step by step {.smaller}

```{r fo-setup}
#| echo: false
f3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
show0 <- function(m) { out <- ifelse(m == 0, "", f3(m)); dimnames(out) <- dimnames(m); out }
Ysp <- sum(d$Y$Y[d$Y$j == "SP"])
fo_row <- d$N |> filter(j == "SP") |> summarise(N = sum(N), .by = "l") |>
  mutate(Y = Ysp, P = f3(N / Ysp)) |> arrange(desc(N))
P2 <- P1 %*% P1
```

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
**1. One row**: patients in `SP` today

```{r fo-row}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(fo_row, col.names = c("tomorrow", "moves N", "at risk Y", "P = N / Y"), align = "lrrr")
```

$\hat P_{j\ell} = \dfrac{\sum_s N_{j\ell}(s)}{\sum_s Y_j(s-1)}$: moves from $j$ to $\ell$ over patient-days at risk in $j$, all days pooled.
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
**2. Every row: the matrix $\hat{\mathbf P}$** (rows = today, columns = tomorrow; blank = impossible; each row sums to 1)

```{r fo-matrix}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(show0(P1), align = "r")
```
:::
:::

::: {.key}
**3. Chapman–Kolmogorov.** In `SP` today, probability of `NIMV` in **2 days**: sum over every possible state $k$ tomorrow,
$P^{(2)}_{\text{SP},\text{NIMV}} = \sum_k P_{\text{SP},k}\,P_{k,\text{NIMV}}$
= `r f3(P1["SP", "SP"])` × `r f3(P1["SP", "NIMV"])` (SP → SP → NIMV) + `r f3(P1["SP", "NIMV"])` × `r f3(P1["NIMV", "NIMV"])` (SP → NIMV → NIMV)
= **`r f3(P2["SP", "NIMV"])`**. In matrix form, $\mathbf P(2) = \mathbf P \cdot \mathbf P$ and $\mathbf P(n) = \mathbf P^{\,n}$.
:::

## Is the present enough?

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.box}
**Patient A**: yesterday `NSP`, today `SP`

*has just worsened to severe pneumonia*
:::
:::
::: {.column width="4%"}
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.box}
**Patient B**: yesterday `SP`, today `SP`

*has had severe pneumonia for some days*
:::
:::
:::

<br>

| | First order | From the data, by yesterday's state |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| P(`NIMV` tomorrow), patient A | `r pct(p1_nimv)` | **`r pct(e_nsp$p)`** (`r pct(e_nsp$lower)`–`r pct(e_nsp$upper)`) |
| P(`NIMV` tomorrow), patient B | `r pct(p1_nimv)` | **`r pct(e_sp$p)`** (`r pct(e_sp$lower)`–`r pct(e_sp$upper)`) |

::: {.note}
The first-order model gives both patients the same probability. The data say patient A is
**`r round(e_nsp$p / e_sp$p)` times** more likely to need non-invasive ventilation tomorrow: the first-order value is an
average of two very different groups, and represents neither.
:::

## Ways to let the past matter

| Approach | Memory added | In practice |
|---|---|---|
| Semi-Markov (clock reset) | time already spent in the current state | continuous time; does not use the previous state |
| Expanding the state space | e.g. "`SP`, first day" and "`SP`, later days" | chosen by hand, state by state |
| Previous state as a covariate | the previous state, in each transition's hazard model | transition by transition; multi-step prediction needs extra modelling |
| **Second-order Markov chain** | **the state at the previous time, for every state** | **systematic; still a Markov chain (on pairs of states)** |

<br>

::: {.key}
The second-order model is the smallest step beyond first order that

1. lets the previous state change **every** transition probability,
2. keeps the counting-process estimators and the Chapman–Kolmogorov predictions of the first-order model, and
3. contains the first-order model as a **special case**.
:::

## Second-order Markov models

$$
P_{hj\ell} = P\big(X_s = \ell \mid X_{s-1} = j,\; X_{s-2} = h\big)
$$

$h$: state at the **previous** time · $j$: state at the **current** time · $\ell$: state at the **next** time · $(h, j)$: the **history**.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Assumptions**

1. Discrete time (here, days).
2. Second order: earlier states are irrelevant.
3. Time homogeneity: $P_{hj\ell}$ does not depend on $s$.
4. Independent individuals.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Price**: more parameters.

With $M$ states, up to $M(M-1)$ first-order probabilities against $M^2(M-1)$ second-order ones.
In DIVINE: **`r n_first`** first-order and **`r nrow(fit$estimate)`** second-order estimated probabilities.
:::
:::

::: {.key}
In DIVINE each state is visited once, so $h \neq j$ means **"first day in $j$"** and $h = j$ means **"two days or more in $j$"**.
:::

## Still a Markov chain, on pairs

The pair $Z_s = (X_{s-1}, X_s)$ is a **first-order** chain, with transition matrix

$$
Q_{(a,b) \to (b,c)} = P_{abc}.
$$

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Estimation**: the relative probability estimator (RPE) pools the second-order counts of each history:

$$
\tilde P_{hj\ell} = \frac{\sum_s \tilde N_{hj\ell}(s)}{\sum_s \tilde Y_{hj}(s-1)}
$$
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Prediction**: the extended Chapman–Kolmogorov relation, by multiplying the distribution of the pair by $Q$ once per step:

$$
P_{hj\ell}(1, n) = P\big(X_{n+1} = \ell \mid X_1 = j,\, X_0 = h\big)
$$
:::
:::

::: {.key}
**First order is the special case** $P_{hj\ell} = P_{j\ell}$ for every $h$: pooling the second-order counts over $h$
gives back $\hat P_{j\ell}$.
:::

## Example: second order, step by step {.smaller}

```{r so-setup}
#| echo: false
Yns <- sum(d$Y$Y[d$Y$h == "NSP" & d$Y$j == "SP"])
so_row <- d$N |> filter(h == "NSP", j == "SP") |> summarise(N = sum(N), .by = "l") |>
  mutate(Y = Yns, P = f3(N / Yns)) |> arrange(desc(N))
# Q[(a, b) -> (b, c)] = P[b, c, a]: an excerpt with three pairs today
pairs_from <- list(c("NSP", "SP"), c("SP", "SP"), c("SP", "NIMV"))
pairs_to   <- list(c("SP", "SP"), c("SP", "NIMV"), c("SP", "IMV"), c("NIMV", "NIMV"), c("NIMV", "IMV"), c("NIMV", "Recov"))
Qx <- sapply(pairs_to, \(t) sapply(pairs_from, \(f) if (f[2] == t[1]) fit$P[t[1], t[2], f[1]] else 0))
dimnames(Qx) <- list(sapply(pairs_from, \(f) sprintf("(%s, %s)", f[1], f[2])),
                     sapply(pairs_to,   \(t) sprintf("(%s, %s)", t[1], t[2])))
a1 <- fit$P["SP", "SP", "NSP"];   a2 <- fit$P["SP", "NIMV", "SP"]
b1 <- fit$P["SP", "NIMV", "NSP"]; b2 <- fit$P["NIMV", "NIMV", "SP"]
ck2 <- ckequations(fit, h = "NSP", j = "SP", l = "NIMV", nsteps = 2)[2]
```

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
**1. RPE for one history**: yesterday `NSP`, today `SP`

```{r so-rpe}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(so_row, col.names = c("tomorrow", "moves Ñ", "at risk Ỹ", "P̃ = Ñ / Ỹ"), align = "lrrr")
```

Same recipe as first order, but **one row per history** $(h, j)$.
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
**2. Those rows are rows of $Q$** (pair today → pair tomorrow), $Q_{(a,b)\to(b,c)} = P_{abc}$; an excerpt

```{r so-q}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(show0(Qx), align = "r")
```

From $(a, b)$ you can only go to pairs that start with $b$ (blank: impossible).
:::
:::

**3. Prediction (Chapman–Kolmogorov on pairs)**: patient A (yesterday `NSP`, today `SP`), probability of `NIMV` in 2 days

| Path | Day 1 | Day 2 (uses the **new** pair) | Product |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| SP → SP → NIMV | $\tilde P_{\text{NSP,SP,SP}}$ = `r f3(a1)` | $\tilde P_{\text{SP,SP,NIMV}}$ = `r f3(a2)` | `r f3(a1 * a2)` |
| SP → NIMV → NIMV | $\tilde P_{\text{NSP,SP,NIMV}}$ = `r f3(b1)` | $\tilde P_{\text{SP,NIMV,NIMV}}$ = `r f3(b2)` | `r f3(b1 * b2)` |
| **Total** | | | **`r f3(a1 * a2 + b1 * b2)`** |

## The `mstate2` package: what each function does {.smaller}

| Function | Input | What it does | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `msprep2()` | sojourn, wide (`Surv()`) or `msdata` | builds the daily panel `(id, time, state)`; reports every change | `msm2prep` |
| `rnd()` | numbers | rounds half away from zero (used for durations) | numbers |
| `prep2()` | daily panel | forms the triples $(h, j, \ell)$ and counts $\tilde N_{hj\ell}(s)$, $\tilde Y_{hj}(s-1)$ | `msm2data` |
| `P2est()` | `msm2data` | RPE, standard errors, Wald or logit intervals; tensor `P[j, l, h]` | `P2est` |
| `P2boot()` | `msm2data` | resamples whole patients and re-estimates $B$ times | `P2boot` |
| `ckequations()` | fit or tensor | $n$-step probabilities, with evolution or bootstrap intervals | matrix / tibble |
| `compare2()` | fit | $n$-step curves for several previous states, with intervals | `msm2pred` |
| `overlap_step()` | `msm2pred` | first step at which the intervals overlap | list |

```r
remotes::install_github("jcarmezim/mstate2")
```

## `msprep2()`: from the data to the daily panel

<div class="sig">msprep2(data, states, trans, durations, outcome, id = "id", keep, unit = 1)</div>

```{r msprep2}
names(MSM)                                            # one row per patient
segs <- c(NSP = "t.nosp", SP = "t.sp", NIMV = "t.nimv", IMV = "t.mv", Recov = "t.recov")
absb <- c(Disch = "disch.s", Death = "death.s")
x <- msprep2(MSM, durations = segs, outcome = absb,
             states = c("NSP", "SP", "Recov", "NIMV", "IMV", "Disch", "Death"))
x
```

::: {.key}
**What it does**: rounds each duration (`rnd()`), repeats each state as many days as it lasts, appends the absorbing
state and returns the daily panel `x$panel`. Unused columns (`inistat`) are kept.
:::

## `msprep2()`: three layouts, one panel {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Wide** data, as `mstate::msprep()`, with one `Surv()` per state:

```r
msprep2(ebmt3,
        states = list(Tx       = NULL,
                      PR       = Surv(prtime, prstat),
                      RelDeath = Surv(rfstime, rfsstat)),
        trans  = c("Tx -> PR -> RelDeath", "Tx -> RelDeath"))
```

An **`msdata`** object made by `mstate::msprep()`:

```r
msprep2(msbmt)
```

**Sojourn** data, as DIVINE: `durations` and `outcome`. With `unit`, continuous times are grouped
into days, weeks or months.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
Nothing is changed silently: every dropped or modified record is listed in `$issues`.

| Issue | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `missing` | status without time, or time without status |
| `rounded_to_zero` | a stay that rounds to 0 units |
| `same_unit` | two states in the same unit |
| `after_absorbing` | a state after the absorbing one |
| `not_allowed` | a move not in `trans` (kept) |
| `no_data` | no usable record |
:::
:::

## `prep2()`: the second-order counts

<div class="sig">prep2(data, id = "id", time = "time", state = "state", states, absorbing, drop.na = FALSE, check.consecutive = TRUE)</div>

::: {.tiny}
```{r prep2}
d <- prep2(x)
d
expo <- summary(d)
```
:::

## `P2est()`: the relative probability estimator

<div class="sig">P2est(object, conf.level = 0.95, ci = c("wald", "logit"), clip = TRUE)</div>

```{r p2est}
fit <- P2est(d)
fit$estimate |> filter(j == "SP")
```

::: {.key}
**What it does**: one row per $(h, j, \ell)$ with estimate, binomial standard error, interval, transitions and
patient-days at risk; the tensor `fit$P[j, l, h]` holds the same estimates. `ci = "logit"` keeps intervals inside $(0, 1)$.
:::

## `P2boot()`: bootstrap of patients

<div class="sig">P2boot(object, B = 200, conf.level = 0.95, seed = NULL)</div>

```{r p2boot}
system.time(bt <- P2boot(d, B = 500, seed = 1))
bt$estimate |> filter(j == "SP") |> select(h, l, p, se, se.boot)
```

::: {.key}
**What it does**: resamples whole patients (the independent units, not their days) and re-estimates everything in each
replicate. Every function that takes a `P2est` also takes a `P2boot`, and then uses percentile bootstrap intervals.
:::

## `ckequations()`: where will the patient be in $n$ days?

<div class="sig">ckequations(x, h, j, l = NULL, nsteps = 9, bounds = FALSE)</div>

```{r ck}
round(ckequations(fit, h = "NSP", j = "SP", nsteps = 7), 3)
ckequations(bt, h = "NSP", j = "SP", l = "NIMV", nsteps = 5, bounds = TRUE)
```

## Same state today, different yesterday

```{r stack}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.9
#| out-width: "100%"
layout(matrix(1:4, 1), widths = c(1, 1, 1, 0.3)); par(cex = 0.9)
stack_plot(ckequations(fit, h = "NSP", j = "SP", nsteps = 20), "SP", "2nd order: NSP -> SP", FALSE)
stack_plot(ckequations(fit, h = "SP",  j = "SP", nsteps = 20), "SP", "2nd order: SP -> SP", FALSE)
stack_plot(ckequations(T1,  h = "SP",  j = "SP", nsteps = 20), "SP", "1st order: SP", FALSE)
state_legend()
```

::: {.key}
Patient A goes through ventilation much more often during the first week than patient B; the first-order prediction
(`T1`: every slice of the tensor equal to the first-order matrix) differs from both.
:::

## `compare2()` and `overlap_step()`: for how long does it matter?

<div class="sig">compare2(object, h, j, l, nsteps = 9, bounds = TRUE) · overlap_step(x)</div>

```{r compare2}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4
#| out-width: "92%"
cmp_nimv <- compare2(fit, h = c("NSP", "SP"), j = "SP", l = "NIMV")
cmp_imv  <- compare2(fit, h = c("NSP", "SP"), j = "SP", l = "IMV")
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(cmp_nimv, dualaxis = FALSE, xlab = "steps (n)", main = "SP -> NIMV")
plot(cmp_imv,  dualaxis = FALSE, xlab = "steps (n)", main = "SP -> IMV")
par(op)
```

::: {.key}
With the evolution intervals, the curves first overlap after **`r overlap_step(cmp_nimv)$n` days** for `NIMV` and
**`r overlap_step(cmp_imv)$n` days** for `IMV` (dotted line): the memory of the previous state lasts about a week.
:::

## `overlap_step()` in detail

```{r overlap}
overlap_step(cmp_nimv)[c("n", "s", "separated_steps", "separation")]
summary(cmp_imv)
```

::: {.key}
**What it returns**: `n`, the first step at which the intervals overlap, and `s = n + 1`, the corresponding time;
`separated_steps`; and `separation` $= \max(L_1, L_2) - \min(U_1, U_2)$ at each step, positive while the intervals are apart.
:::

## Bootstrap intervals

::: {.tiny}
```{r compare2-boot}
#| output-location: column
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 3.9
cmp_b <- compare2(bt, h = c("NSP", "SP"),
                  j = "SP", l = "NIMV")
summary(cmp_b)
plot(cmp_b, dualaxis = FALSE,
     xlab = "steps (n)", main = "SP -> NIMV")
lines(1:9, ckequations(T1, "SP", "SP", "NIMV"),
      lty = 2, lwd = 2)              # first order
```
:::

::: {.key}
The evolution intervals assume every probability at its limit at once, so they widen quickly; the bootstrap intervals
propagate the joint uncertainty and are narrower. The dashed first-order curve starts between the two histories and
then rises above both: it applies the 5.2% risk of entering `NIMV` on every day in `SP`, while after the first day the real risk is 2.6%.
:::

## Example: evolution vs bootstrap intervals, step by step {.smaller}

```{r ci-setup}
#| echo: false
# Two-day probability of NIMV for patient A (yesterday NSP, today SP): the two paths of the chain on pairs
path1 <- function(T) T["SP", "SP", "NSP"] * T["SP", "NIMV", "SP"]       # SP -> SP -> NIMV
path2 <- function(T) T["SP", "NIMV", "NSP"] * T["NIMV", "NIMV", "SP"]   # SP -> NIMV -> NIMV
show_path <- function(T, f) {
  if (identical(f, path1)) sprintf("%s × %s = %s", f3(T["SP", "SP", "NSP"]), f3(T["SP", "NIMV", "SP"]), f3(f(T)))
  else sprintf("%s × %s = %s", f3(T["SP", "NIMV", "NSP"]), f3(T["NIMV", "NIMV", "SP"]), f3(f(T)))
}
ev_tab <- data.frame(
  path  = c("SP → SP → NIMV", "SP → NIMV → NIMV", "**Total**"),
  lower = c(show_path(fit$P.lower, path1), show_path(fit$P.lower, path2), paste0("**", f3(path1(fit$P.lower) + path2(fit$P.lower)), "**")),
  upper = c(show_path(fit$P.upper, path1), show_path(fit$P.upper, path2), paste0("**", f3(path1(fit$P.upper) + path2(fit$P.upper)), "**")))
rs_lo <- sum(fit$P.lower["SP", , "NSP"]); rs_up <- sum(fit$P.upper["SP", , "NSP"])
# Bootstrap: the same two-day probability in every replicate tensor, then percentiles
rep_day1 <- bt$boot["SP", "NIMV", "NSP", ]
rep_day2 <- apply(bt$boot, 4, \(T) path1(T) + path2(T))
q1 <- quantile(rep_day1, c(0.025, 0.975)); q2 <- quantile(rep_day2, c(0.025, 0.975))
bs_tab <- data.frame(
  replicate = c("1", "2", "3", "…", "500", "**2.5% – 97.5%**"),
  day1 = c(f3(rep_day1[1:3]), "…", f3(rep_day1[500]), sprintf("**%s – %s**", f3(q1[1]), f3(q1[2]))),
  day2 = c(f3(rep_day2[1:3]), "…", f3(rep_day2[500]), sprintf("**%s – %s**", f3(q2[1]), f3(q2[2]))))
ev5 <- ckequations(fit, "NSP", "SP", "NIMV", nsteps = 5, bounds = TRUE)[5, ]
bs5 <- ckequations(bt,  "NSP", "SP", "NIMV", nsteps = 5, bounds = TRUE)[5, ]
```

Patient A (yesterday `NSP`, today `SP`): probability of `NIMV` in **2 days**. Estimate: `r f3(path1(fit$P))` + `r f3(path2(fit$P))` = **`r f3(path1(fit$P) + path2(fit$P))`**.

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Evolution intervals** (`P2est`): the same calculation with **every** probability at its lower limit (`fit$P.lower`), then at its upper limit (`fit$P.upper`)

```{r ci-ev}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(ev_tab, col.names = c("path", "with lower limits", "with upper limits"), align = "lcc")
```

The limit tensors are not probabilities: row (`NSP`, `SP`) sums to `r f3(rs_lo)` in `P.lower` and `r f3(rs_up)` in `P.upper`.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Bootstrap intervals** (`P2boot`): the same calculation in **each** of the 500 resampled tensors, then the percentiles

```{r ci-bs}
#| echo: false
knitr::kable(bs_tab, col.names = c("replicate", "day 1", "day 2"), align = "lcc")
```

Each replicate is a valid tensor (rows sum to 1), so errors partly cancel.
:::
:::

::: {.key}
Day 2: evolution **`r f3(path1(fit$P.lower) + path2(fit$P.lower))` – `r f3(path1(fit$P.upper) + path2(fit$P.upper))`** vs bootstrap **`r f3(q2[1])` – `r f3(q2[2])`**.
Day 5: evolution **`r f3(ev5$lower)` – `r f3(ev5$upper)`** vs bootstrap **`r f3(bs5$lower)` – `r f3(bs5$upper)`**: every step adds the extreme combination
of limits, so evolution intervals widen faster.
:::

## Summary

| Question | Function |
|---|---|
| How do I get a daily panel from my data (including `mstate` data)? | `msprep2()`, `rnd()` |
| What are the second-order counts? | `prep2()`, `summary()` |
| What is $P_{hj\ell}$, with its uncertainty? | `P2est()`, `P2boot()` |
| Where will a patient be in $n$ days? | `ckequations()` |
| Does the previous state matter, and for how long? | `compare2()`, `overlap_step()` |

::: {.key}
**In DIVINE**: patients in `SP` today who were in `NSP` yesterday need ventilation far more often than those already
in `SP`; the difference lasts about a week; and a first-order model averages over histories that behave very differently.
:::
